sources.massKg: typical 2-pax + fuel operating mass, research doc range 950-1050 kg. NOT max gross (1157 kg): the POH V-speeds are quoted at max gross, but hitting them at max gross would require a CLmax outside the sourced 1.47-1.58 range. Documented compromise, decisions.md B-006.
sources.wingAreaM2: JSBSim c172x.xml, cross-checked Roskam (174 sq ft)
sources.clAlphaPerRad: NACA 2412 2D slope with finite-AR correction; JSBSim table range 4.5-4.7
sources.stallAlphaRad: TUNING KNOB (stall speeds) — 15.0 deg, NACA 2412 critical AoA. Implies CLmax_clean = 0.25 + 4.9*0.2618 = 1.533, inside the sourced 1.47-1.58 range, and Vs1 = 48.1 KCAS against the POH's 48. Verified by envelope.test.ts.
sources.postStallDecayRad: TUNING KNOB — 0.20 rad (11.5 deg) fade width from CLmax toward flat-plate lift past the break. Gives the soft mushy stall the 172 is known for (about 15% CL lost in the first 2 deg past the break); smaller is a sharper CL cliff. Does NOT move CLmax.
sources.cd0: TUNING KNOB (cruise + top speed) — raised from the JSBSim book value 0.032 to 0.035. Measured by envelope.test.ts: 75% rated power at 8000 ft settles at 123.4 kt TAS (POH 122-124, band 117-127) and sea-level full power tops out at 128.1 kt TAS (POH Vh 126, band 118-134). Real CD0 is unpublished.
sources.gearDragCd0: 0 — the 172 has fixed gear; its drag is already inside the sourced cd0 (0.035). Present so the field is required data everywhere, per GR-003, not a per-class branch.
sources.speedbrakeCd0: 0 — the C172 has no speedbrake/spoiler; KeyB is inert. Present so the field is required data everywhere (#51), not a per-class branch.
sources.oswaldE: TUNING KNOB — 0.70, derived from a published C172 model (CD0=0.0329, K=0.0599).
sources.cyBeta: textbook light-single side-force slope; makes a slip cost energy
sources.rollRateMaxRadS: 40 deg/s — middle of the research doc's 30-45 deg/s light-GA estimate
sources.pitchRateMaxRadS: 20 deg/s — TUNING KNOB, no published figure
sources.yawRateMaxRadS: 15 deg/s — TUNING KNOB, no published figure
sources.damping/stiffness: TUNING KNOBS. Pitch: omega_n = sqrt(3.0) = 1.73 rad/s, zeta = 2.5/(2*1.73) = 0.72 — a well-damped short period.
sources.refDynamicPressurePa: TUNING KNOB — 1200 Pa (~44 m/s at sea level). Controls scale with q/qref, clamped to 1, so authority fades toward the stall.
sources.trimAlphaCenterRad: 1.0 deg — near the cruise AoA so trim = 0 is roughly hands-off cruise
sources.propPeakSpeedMs: TUNING KNOB (climb, without disturbing cruise — it only bites below 60 m/s and cruise is above it) — 60 m/s (117 kt). Below it, prop efficiency falls linearly, which both caps static thrust at eta*P/60 = 1790 N (402 lbf) and brings sea-level best climb from an absurd 1708 fpm down to a measured 783 fpm against the POH's 730 fpm (envelope.test.ts band 630-830).
sources.lapseModel: "piston" — the IO-360 is normally aspirated, so forces.ts applies the Gagg-Ferrar lapse P(h)/P(0) = (sigma-0.117)/0.883 to maxPowerW. Selected by this key rather than assumed, so a flat-rated turbofan class can ship "none" without a per-class branch; an absent or unknown value is a load-time validator error, never a silent default. Added in Task 3: without the lapse, best climb at the 14000 ft service ceiling is 971 fpm, i.e. no ceiling at all; with it, 210 fpm. Consequence: the POH's '75% power at 8000 ft' needs 99.0% throttle, since the lapse there is 0.758.
sources.vnoIasMs: 129 KIAS = 66.36 m/s, 172S POH max structural cruising speed. Top of the ASI green arc / bottom of the yellow caution band. Not a tuning knob and not used by the physics - display only.
sources.vfeIasMs: 85 KIAS = 43.73 m/s, 172S POH max flaps-extended speed for the 10-30 deg range (the 10 deg-only limit is 110 KIAS; the ASI white arc uses the more restrictive figure, which is what the arc means). Top of the ASI white arc. Display only.
sources.flaps: 172S has 0/10/20/30 detents. dCL0 (0 / 0.3 / 0.6 / 0.9) is a TUNING KNOB for the stall speeds: flaps-30 CLmax = (0.25 + 0.9) + 4.9*0.2094 = 2.176, measured Vs0 = 40.4 KCAS against the POH's 40 (band 37-43), with Vs 48.1 / 45.1 / 42.5 / 40.4 kt falling monotonically across the detents. dCD0 values are TUNING KNOBS.
sources.gear: fixed — the 172 has no retractable gear; the HUD reads FIXED and G is inert
sources.afterburnerFactor: 1.0 — the IO-360 has no afterburner. Required in every params file so a jet class can ship a real dry→wet factor without a per-class branch; 1.0 leaves thrustNewtons unchanged.
sources.mmo: 0.45 — a value the C172 never reaches (Vh 126 kt TAS at SL is M0.19; at the 14000 ft ceiling still under M0.25). Present only so the Mach annunciator is data everywhere, per spec §2.3; not a real placard limit.
sources.vleIasMs: 83.85 m/s — set equal to vneIasMs, so IAS can never exceed it (structurally unreachable even before the retractable-only GEAR O'SPD gate excludes fixed gear entirely, GR-004).
sources.display: ASI face 40–180 kt is the existing C172 gauge range (Vs0 40.4 to Vne 163 with headroom); attitudeStyle "line" keeps the minimalist horizon. Jets override both.
sources.lookArc: // tunable — GA-piston family (issue #44 follow-up): wing struts and a low door sill limit how far you can crane your neck. yawDeg 100 either side, pitchUpDeg 40 (headliner), pitchDownDeg 25 (panel/floor).
